headers.comment: The ENTRY POINT must never outlive the hashed chunks it names. Firebase's default for index.html is max-age=3600, while the chunks below are immutable for a year - so a deploy that rotates a bundle hash leaves every browser that loaded in the previous hour asking for a file the same deploy deleted, and the sandbox iframe dies on a 404 until the hour is up. A parent hard-reload does NOT rescue it: Chrome partitions its HTTP cache by top-level site, so the stale copy is only reachable from the page that is broken by it. `no-cache` still stores the file and still 304s on the ETag; it just refuses to serve it without asking first, which is the only setting under which content-hashed assets are safe to delete.
